definitions.explanation: An organized arrangement of people standing or moving in orderly lines, especially in military or ceremonial contexts.

examples.japanese: {隊列|たいれつ}を{組|く}んで{行進|こうしん}する。
{子|こ}どもたちが{隊列|たいれつ}を{作|つく}って{歩|ある}いていた。
examples.english: The children were walking in a line.

examples.japanese: {兵士|へいし}たちは{整然|せいぜん}とした{隊列|たいれつ}で{広場|ひろば}を{横切|よこぎ}った。
examples.english: The soldiers crossed the square in orderly formation.

notes:
Composed of {隊|たい} (group, squad) + {列|れつ} (row, line). Implies organized, purposeful arrangement of people in lines or columns, carrying a sense of order and discipline.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {隊列|たいれつ}を{組|く}む: to form a line/formation
- {隊列|たいれつ}を{作|つく}る: to make a formation
- {隊列|たいれつ}を{乱|みだ}す: to break formation; to disrupt the ranks
- {隊列|たいれつ}を{整|ととの}える: to straighten the formation
- {隊列|たいれつ}{行進|こうしん}: marching in formation

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {行列|ぎょうれつ}: line; queue; procession — a general word for people lined up, often waiting. {隊列|たいれつ} implies more military discipline and organization.
- {列|れつ}: row; line — the most basic word for a line of people or things. {隊列|たいれつ} specifically implies a group moving or standing in organized formation.
- {縦隊|じゅうたい}: column (military) — a specific formation type where people are lined up front to back.
